name: Education and Teacher Certification
degree: Teacher certification in addition to a departmental or interdisciplinary major (no separate degree stated)

requirements.label: language
requirements.title: Language other than English

rule.text: One year of a language other than English at the college level on a transcript of record with grades of "C" or better. May be met through American Sign Language as well as foreign languages. Some majors have more extensive language requirements.
rule.reason: Language study is described by level and grade, not by a fixed course list, so it cannot be matched to specific course codes.

requirements.sourceText: All teacher candidates must have one year of a language other than English at the college level on a transcript of record with grades of "C" or better. This requirement may be met through the study of American Sign Language as well as foreign languages. Please note that some majors have more extensive language requirements.

requirements.label: content-credits
requirements.title: Content field credits

rule.manualCheck: Verify with the program director for the certification content area that at least 36 content-field credits are completed.
rule.text: Complete all requirements of the chosen academic major, with a minimum of 36 credits in the content field required for teacher certification.
rule.reason: The content field is defined by each academic department and is not listed by course in this catalog section.

requirements.sourceText: Students must complete all requirements of their chosen academic major, with a minimum of 36 credits in the content field required for teacher certification. Stony Brook requirements exceed NYSED requirements in most instances.

requirements.label: fieldwork-student-teaching
requirements.title: Fieldwork and student teaching

rule.manualCheck: Confirm 100 fieldwork hours and 75 days of supervised student teaching, with the listed experience areas, through the program coordinator.
rule.text: 100 hours of fieldwork prior to student teaching, with specific experiences in high-needs districts, ethnic and cultural diversity, inclusion of students with special needs, integration of technology in the curriculum, literacy across all curricula, and other selected topics. Then 75 days of supervised student teaching.
rule.reason: Hours and days of fieldwork and student teaching are not expressible as course counts; the required experiences are not course-coded.

requirements.sourceText: Students must complete all pedagogy credits in the professional study of education (credits vary according to the specific certification program) including foundation and literacy courses, and 100 hours of fieldwork prior to student teaching with specific experiences dealing with areas related to high-needs districts, ethnic and cultural diversity, inclusion of students with special needs, integration of technology in the curriculum, literacy across all curricula, and other selected topics. Students must complete 75 days of supervised student teaching.

requirements.title: Teacher certification program (choose one)

rules.text: All requirements for the major in English with a minimum of 36 credits in the cognate field, including specific course content areas required for accreditation. See Program Director for details.

Admission-level GPA threshold; not a course rule.

rules.manualCheck: Writing sample is reviewed by the program.
rules.text: A writing sample that best reflects the candidate's good writing skills.
rules.reason: Admission document, not a course rule.

rules.text: Completion of the requirements for the major in Asian and Asian American Studies, French, Italian, or Spanish.
rules.reason: Major content is defined by the department and is not listed by course here.

rules.text: Students must complete 36 credit hours of courses in the language to be eligible for certification. Courses taught in English will not satisfy the language requirement for certification purposes.

rules.manualCheck: Verify OPI rating of Advanced-Low (ACTFL 1999 Speaking guidelines) before student teaching.
rules.text: Prior to student teaching, an official ACTFL OPI with a minimum spoken proficiency rating of Advanced-Low.
rules.reason: Proficiency test result, not a course.

rules.reason: Major content is defined by the mathematics department and is not listed in this section.

rules.text: Completion of the requirements for the biology, chemistry, earth and space science or physics major.

rules.sourceText: Social Studies Secondary Teacher Education Program: Requirements for Initial Certification

rules.text: A major in one of the following social science departments: Africana Studies, Anthropology, Economics, History, Political Science, or Sociology.
rules.reason: Major selection is not a course list.

rules.text: A minimum of 48 credits in the social sciences, including courses in the departments mentioned above but excluding psychology, linguistics and multidisciplinary studies. Program-specific requirements must be satisfied within these 48 credits.
rules.reason: Credit pool is defined by department classification and program-specific sub-requirements, not by a fixed course list.

rules.text: Two years of college-level study of a language or languages other than English. Completion of Skill 3/LANG SBC Basic Foreign Language Competence satisfies the first year.
rules.reason: Language study is described by level, not by a fixed course list.

rules.label: TESOL Pre-K–12

requirements.sourceText: Teacher certification programs: English Secondary; Foreign Languages Secondary; Mathematics Secondary; Science Secondary (Biology, Chemistry, Earth Sciences, Physics); Social Studies Secondary; TESOL Pre-K-12. Each program lists its own initial certification requirements, including professional educational requirements.

policies.sourceText: All teacher candidates must have one year of a language other than English at the college level on a transcript of record with grades of "C" or better.

To be eligible to student teach, students must have: a grade of C or higher but with a minimum g.p.a. of 2.75 total in: all courses required for the MAT or AMS major; AMS 310; MAT 336; MAE 301, MAE 302, MAE 311, MAE 312, MAE 447; PSY 327, SSE 350; LIN 344.
a minimum cumulative g.p.a. of 2.75 in all of the mathematics courses listed above, or by permission of the program director.

substitutions.condition: Well-prepared student, with permission of the Director of Mathematics Education
substitutions.sourceText: With the permission of the Director of Mathematics Education, a well-prepared student may substitute MAT 364 for MAT 360.

notes.text: Students must formally apply for admission to one of the six teacher certification programs with the appropriate application, supporting documentation, and declaration of major form. An essay of 500-750 words on a topic germane to education is required. Interviews and writing samples may also be required. Registration in methods and other certification courses requires admission to D-TALE. Submitting the application by the end of the sophomore year is recommended.

Mathematics: apply during the second semester of sophomore year or first semester of junior year; applicants need grades of C or higher with an average of at least B in calculus, linear algebra and MAT 200 coursework, and an overall GPA of 3.00. Only open to Mathematics or Applied Mathematics and Statistics majors.

TESOL: must major in Linguistics with a 3.00 overall GPA and 3.00 in the major. Application due April 15 (Fall) and November 15 (Spring). Foreign Languages, Sciences and Social Studies programs are each open only to students in specified majors.

Courses taken for Pass/No Credit may not be used to satisfy the preparation in professional education component of any Teacher Education Program. Social Studies: Pass/No Credit courses may not be used toward the 48-credit social science requirement.

Students should maintain a cumulative GPA of 3.00 to remain in good standing. Professional education courses may only be repeated once. A grade below C in certain methodology courses, the student teaching seminar, foundations or literacy courses requires repetition or satisfactory completion before advancing.

Students must complete all courses required for the major, cognate fields, and professional licensure before student teaching. Foreign Languages, Mathematics and Social Studies require a 3.00 GPA for student teaching, with exceptions at the discretion of the program director.
Spanish: choose SPN 462, SPN 463 or SPN 465 in satisfying major Requirement A.5. Consult departmental teacher education advisors for content requirements.
French/Italian and Chinese/Japanese/Korean secondary programs have no separate course list on this page; students should consult the appropriate departmental advisors.

Science: students must have declared a major in biology, chemistry, earth and space science or physics, added the teacher preparation option, and completed at least four science laboratory courses before taking SCI 410 / SCI 449.
General Science (grades 7-12) extension: 18 semester hours in two or more sciences other than the primary licensed science. Optional extension; not a separate requirement.

Certification is not automatic. After the program, students must apply to NYSED via TEACH, complete child abuse, substance abuse, school violence, DASA and fingerprinting requirements, pass NYSTCE exams, and submit a FERPA Release Form to the Teacher Certification Office.

Combined bachelor's/master's teacher preparation programs allow up to 15 graduate credits shared with the undergraduate degree (8 for BA/MA in TESOL, 12 for BA/MA in English, 6 for BA in History with the M.A. in History). Accelerated degree programs leading to certification are not offered. Options are not evaluated here.
